## Why This Is Asked

Tests for media streaming must handle real-world conditions like fluctuating networks, ABR behavior, offline capabilities, and resume after restarts. This question probes how a candidate structures a deterministic E2E that exercises client-side playback state, CDN mocking, and cross-device consistency.

## Key Concepts

- E2E testing of streaming with ABR and buffering dynamics
- Network throttling and telemetry-based assertions
- Offline caching and resume playback from cache
- Test data isolation and deterministic CDN manifests

## Code Example

```javascript
// Playwright test skeleton for ABR and offline caching
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'

test('streaming ABR and offline resume', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('https://streaming.example.com')
  await page.fill('#email', 'test+stream@example.com')
  await page.fill('#password', 'password')
  await page.click('#signin')
  await page.click('.title-card[data-title="Show1"]')
  await page.click('#play')
  // simulate network changes and verify telemetry events
  // offline download flow
  await page.click('#download-offline')
  // restart and resume
  await page.reload()
  await page.click('#resume')
  // basic assertions
  expect(await page.locator('#player').isVisible()).toBeTruthy()
})
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend this to verify synchronized playback across multiple devices?
- What metrics would you collect to quantify user-perceived latency during ABR transitions?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests at beginner level need practical E2E coverage for mobile, data isolation, and flaky networks in beginner-friendly scope.

- Test data seeding and isolation
- End-to-end booking flow
- External service mocking (payments)
- Retry and flakiness handling

## Code Example

```javascript
// Example Cypress sketch (conceptual)
describe('Booking flow end-to-end', () => {
  it('searches, books, and confirms a booking', () => {
    cy.viewport(375, 812)
    cy.exec('node scripts/seed_test_data.js city listings=3')
    cy.intercept('POST', '/payments/*', { statusCode: 200, body: { status: 'success' } }).as('pay')
    cy.visit('/search?city=SampleCity')
    cy.get('#filters').select('Under $200')
    cy.get('.listing').first().click()
    cy.get('#book').click()
    cy.get('#checkout').type('4242424242424242')
    cy.get('#pay').click()
    cy.wait('@pay')
    cy.get('.upcoming-trips').should('contain', 'SampleCity')
  })
})
```

- How would you adapt for a non-PCI DSS environment?
- How would you validate data consistency if the payment gateway is slow or retries?

This question probes realism around feature flags and canary rollouts, emphasizing runtime toggling, deterministic segmentation, and end-to-end integrity across UI and backend boundaries. It also assesses how to design deterministic tests in a dynamic release scenario.

## Key Concepts

- Feature flags and canary rollout semantics
- Runtime toggling without full page reload
- Deterministic user seeding and segmentation
- E2E coverage across desktop/mobile
- Data isolation for reusable test seeds

## Code Example

```javascript
// Playwright pseudo-snippet: intercept canary flag and route UI
const flagApi = '/flags/newCheckout'
await page.route(flagApi, route => {
  route.fulfill({ status: 200, body: JSON.stringify({ enabled: true, canaryPercent: 10 }) })
})
// visit checkout and assert NEW UI present for canary users
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you scale this to multiple canary percentages (e.g., 10%, 50%, 90%)?
- How do you guard against flakiness when the canary decision is client-side vs server-side?

## Key Concepts
- Real-time WebSocket delivery
- Offline/online transitions
- Eventual consistency
- Idempotency and deduplication
- Test data isolation

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests for real-time user journeys with WebSocket are notoriously flaky. This question probes your ability to design deterministic E2E flows, manage data isolation, and handle network resilience.

## Key Concepts
- Real-time UI updates via WebSocket
- Event deduplication and idempotent retry logic
- Test data seeding and environment isolation
- Mocking network/WebSocket for deterministic test execution
- CI-friendly timing strategies to reduce flakiness
- Client reconnection and error recovery behavior
